comment: small->little: acceptable synonym, no error.
wires->cables: acceptable synonym, no error.
glue->adhesive: synonym, meaning preserved, but slightly stilted register for a kid-level DIY sentence; not flagged as an error, naturalness nudged down.
how much->how far: acceptable paraphrase, both read naturally as degree/distance of motor movement.
certain->specific: acceptable synonym, no error.
series->sequence: acceptable synonym, no error.
dropped article 'a'.
about->for subtly shifts topic to purpose; still readable.
present->past tense shift, clearly wrong for the generic-instruction register of the passage.
is->are agreement error.
third->fourth breaks the motor count sequence (skips from 'another' to 'fourth'), a clear factual slip.
wrong particle; meaning close but changed.

errors.learner_form: move him to a new spot
errors.corrected_form: move them to a new spot

comment: them->him: wrong number/gender, no sensible antecedent for 'him', clearly wrong but the intended meaning is recoverable.

errors.learner_form: It tells the motors to move.
errors.corrected_form: It tells the motors when to move.

comment: 'when' dropped, loses the timing/coordination sense that the next sentence ('how much to move') pairs with.
'also' inserted redundantly; 'you'->'everyone' shifts addressee from the reader to a general audience.
homophone typo, obviously a slip, still readable.

errors.learner_form: It says the motors when to move
errors.corrected_form: It tells the motors when to move

comment: 'says' does not take this object/complement structure ('says the motors when...'); reads as clearly wrong/ungrammatical to a native speaker, not just a lexical nuance.

errors.learner_form: Then another motor you can tell to move.
errors.corrected_form: Then you can tell another motor to move.

comment: OSV scrambling, ungrammatical word order but meaning recoverable.
dialectal/informal 'y'all' clashes with the neutral instructional register of the rest of the passage.
can->cannot inverts the sentence's meaning entirely.

errors.learner_form: Another motor can't make it move
errors.corrected_form: Another motor can make it move

comment: can->can't inverts capability claim.

errors.learner_form: move them from a new spot
errors.corrected_form: move them to a new spot

comment: to->from reverses the direction of the action (destination becomes origin).
many->few is a quantity inversion, opposite claim.

errors.learner_form: The Arduino writes instructions for you.
errors.corrected_form: You write instructions for the Arduino.

comment: agent and recipient are swapped, reversing who does the instructing.
later->first reverses the intended progression from simple to complex.
90->9 changes the illustrative example's number; the example sentence stays fully grammatical and its teaching point (syntax of the command) is intact.

errors.learner_form: you can avoid simple sticks and glue
errors.corrected_form: you can use simple sticks and glue

comment: use->avoid reverses the advice given.
'servo engines' is not a real term (servos are motors, not engines); a small factual/terminology slip, still understandable.

errors.learner_form: But you can tell another motor
errors.corrected_form: Then you can tell another motor

comment: Then->But swaps a sequencing connective for a contrastive one with no real contrast present.

errors.learner_form: Also, you need an Arduino board
errors.corrected_form: First, you need an Arduino board

comment: First->Also loses the ordinal/sequencing signal that opens the list of parts needed.
gripper->thing flattens a specific, meaningful technical term into a vague generic word, losing real information about the robot part.
commands->stuff flattens the specific programming term into a vague generic word.

errors.learner_form: This DIY project teaches about electronics.
errors.corrected_form: This DIY project teaches you about electronics.

errors.learner_form: You learned how to connect wires.
errors.corrected_form: You learn how to connect wires.

comment: four independent grammar slips stacked in one short passage: dropped article, dropped object 'you', wrong tense, wrong agreement.

errors.learner_form: Then another motor you can tell to move.
errors.corrected_form: Then you can tell another motor to move.

comment: plural dropped on 'command'; 'position'->'spot' alone is an acceptable synonym so not flagged, but the appended slang tag ', yo' is a jarring register break; final sentence scrambled to OSV order.
important->expensive substitutes an unrelated attribute, clearly wrong; pick up->pick out is a minor wrong-particle phrasal-verb slip.
